# Balance & Steady Feet: how it works {: .nobreak}

<div class="chang" markdown="1">
<div class="who">Chang Yin</div>

I'm Chang. AI character. Twelve weeks, one program, done properly. Otago-style leg strength and balance practice plus simplified tai chi, to help you feel steadier on your feet.

A little more, slowly. That's the whole method.
</div>


**Who it's for.** Adults 60+ who want to feel steadier on their feet and more confident on stairs, curbs and uneven ground. Every exercise is done at the kitchen counter.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Ask your doctor first if:</span> Dizziness or fainting, a fall with injury or head strike (especially on blood thinners), sudden new unsteadiness, or new numbness: see your doctor first. Using a walker: start at Rebuild, with both hands on the counter.
</div>


**What you need.** Kitchen counter, sturdy chair against a wall, a rolled bath towel, stairs with a rail (optional), shoes with grippy soles.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Every day:</span> Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain. Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now. Pain rule (E41): Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
</div>




## Your week

Mon: strength · Tue: program session A · Wed: balance · Thu: program session B · Fri: breath + qigong · Sat: walk-and-talk · Sun: rest + stretch. Program sessions are marked in **bold** in the plan; the other days use your Strong Years Daily Practice sessions (DP numbers).

## How it progresses

Three 4-week phases: **Foundation** (weeks 1–4, A1/B1), **Build** (weeks 5–8, A2/B2) and **Strengthen** (weeks 9–12, A3/B3).

| Week in each phase | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1st | Doses as written in the session. Learn the moves. Stop each set with one or two good reps left in the tank. |
| 2nd | Add 1–2 reps per set (never past 12). Holds up 5 seconds (never past 30). |
| 3rd | Where every rep felt easy two sessions in a row, use the Harder version or a heavier jug. Otherwise repeat week 2. |
| 4th (easy week) | Easy week: same moves, one set fewer. Then do your checkpoint at the weekend. |

**Levels.** Every session has four versions: Rebuild (chair-based), Steady, Strong and Iron. Move up only when every rep felt easy two sessions in a row. Move down any day. **Advanced** doses are never a starting point.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Red flags:</span> Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
</div>




# Your checkpoints

Start, then the end of weeks 4, 8 and 12. Same chair, same shoes, same time of day. These are fitness checks from published research, **not medical tests**.

<table class="write small"><thead><tr><th>Checkpoint</th><th>How</th><th>Start</th><th>Week 4</th><th>Week 8</th><th>Week 12</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Four-stage balance</strong> (E50)</td><td>Last stage held 10 s (0–4). Under 10 s on heel-to-toe is worth mentioning to your doctor (CDC screening checkpoint)</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Timed Up and Go</strong> (E51)</td><td>Seconds, normal pace, helper beside you. 12 s or more = tell your doctor</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>One-leg stand</strong> (E09)</td><td>Seconds up to 30, hand hovering over the counter, each leg</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>30-second chair stand</strong> (E11)</td><td>Full stands</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Confidence on your feet</strong> (self-rating)</td><td>0–10: stairs, curbs, getting up at night, walking on grass</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>We live at the counter. Hands hover, they don't wander.</td><td>Hands hover, they don't wander</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:20 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly shift your weight to your right foot. Pause.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay flat on the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:20–2:20 · Seated knee straightening

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated knee straightening</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Straighten your right knee until your leg is level, or as close as you can.</td><td>Easier: Straighten halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point to the ceiling.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze, then lower slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you straighten your leg.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Toes point to the ceiling. Squeeze, then lower slowly. **Easier:** Straighten only halfway. **Harder:** Hold for 5 seconds at the top, or add a light ankle weight later.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:20–3:10 · Side steps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Side steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step sideways to the right, then bring your left foot to meet it.</td><td>Easier: Fewer, slower steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stay tall.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small, controlled steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally. Talk or count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stay tall. Small, controlled steps. Feet don't cross. **Easier:** Fewer steps, slower. **Harder:** Bend your knees slightly and stay low, or tie a resistance loop above your knees.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:10–4:20 · Heel-to-toe stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel-to-toe stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toe.</td><td>Easier: Half-step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes on something still at eye level.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft knees. Tall head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly and steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes on something still at eye level. Soft knees. Tall head. **Easier:** Half-step stance: front foot's heel beside the big toe of the back foot. Both hands on the counter. **Harder:** Lift one hand to hover just above the counter. Later: both hands hovering.

**Safety callouts:** Balance drills always start with support. Hands hover, they don't wander away from the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:20–5:30 · One-leg stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>One-leg stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to your left foot.</td><td>Easier: Toe stays on the floor</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly. Count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg. **Easier:** Just shift your weight onto one foot, keeping the other toe lightly on the floor. **Harder:** One hand hovering above the counter, then both hands hovering, right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:30–6:30 · Heel-to-toe walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel-to-toe walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step forward, placing your heel directly in front of the toes of the other foot.</td><td>Easier: Feet apart, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes forward, not down at your feet.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow is correct.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes forward, not down at your feet. Slow is correct. **Easier:** Walk with your feet slightly apart, not touching, holding the counter. **Harder:** Let your hand hover above the counter. Later: walk backward along the counter with one hand resting on it (normal steps).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:30–7:30 · Toe and heel walks

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Toe and heel walks</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise onto the balls of your feet.</td><td>Easier: Heel raises in place</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall. Small steps. **Easier:** Heel raises in place instead. **Harder:** Hand hovering, still right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:30–8:15 · Sit-to-stand, no hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Sit-to-stand, no hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit with feet slightly narrower than usual.</td><td>Easier: Hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Find your balance at the top before you move.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Find your balance at the top before you move. Slow down. **Easier:** Use your hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Feet together.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:15–8:50 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:50–9:15 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Steady feet are trained feet.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toothbrush balance tonight. Hand on the sink.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<tr><td>6:15–7:15</td><td><strong>Holding up the sky</strong><br>Holding up the sky (baduanjin piece 1)</td><td>4 reps, seated</td><td>5 reps</td><td>6 reps</td><td>6 reps, rise onto toes</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:15–8:15</td><td><strong>Heel-to-toe stand</strong><br>Heel-to-toe stand at the counter</td><td>2 × 10 seconds each side, half-step</td><td>2 × 15 seconds each side</td><td>2 × 20 seconds each side, hand hovering</td><td>2 × 30 seconds each side, hands hovering</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:15–9:15</td><td><strong>4-6 breathing</strong></td><td>1 minute</td><td>1 minute</td><td>1 minute</td><td>1 minute</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:15–9:40</td><td><strong>Close</strong></td><td colspan="4">All levels together</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tai chi day. Taught as exercise.</td><td>Balance · B1</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tai chi is slow balance practice: weight shifts, short steps and turns, done with control. We start small.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fence or counter within reach. Chair behind you.</td><td>Slow like honey</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:35–2:35 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly shift your weight to your right foot. Pause.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay flat on the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–4:35 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to the right foot while your right hand floats across in front of your face and your left hand floats low in front of your belly.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:35–6:15 · Brush knee

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Brush knee</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step forward with the left foot, heel first, into a short stance.</td><td>Easier: Arms only, feet together</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short step, not a lunge.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight moves slowly from back foot to front foot.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push forward.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Short step, not a lunge. Weight moves slowly from back foot to front foot. **Easier:** Arms only, feet together, one hand on the counter. **Harder:** Four steps across the room and back, near the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:15–7:15 · Holding up the sky

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Holding up the sky</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in and lift your hands slowly up the front of your body, turning palms to the ceiling as they pass your face.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow, like moving through warm water.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Look straight ahead.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as the hands rise, out as they come down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow, like moving through warm water. Look straight ahead. **Easier:** Sit and do it seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Rise onto your toes a little at the top, holding the chair back with one hand if needed.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:15–8:15 · Heel-to-toe stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel-to-toe stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toe.</td><td>Easier: Half-step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes on something still at eye level.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft knees. Tall head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly and steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes on something still at eye level. Soft knees. Tall head. **Easier:** Half-step stance: front foot's heel beside the big toe of the back foot. Both hands on the counter. **Harder:** Lift one hand to hover just above the counter. Later: both hands hovering.

**Safety callouts:** Balance drills always start with support. Hands hover, they don't wander away from the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:15–9:15 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Belly rises first.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft shoulders.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:15–9:40 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow like honey. Soft knees.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weekend: walk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# BAL-A2 · Phase 2 (Build): Otago steps

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Balance & Steady Feet program | 8:25 | SET-KITCHEN | C-TRAIN-B | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.
</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Phase two. New steps.</td><td>Balance · A2</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Backward, over, around. Every step next to the counter.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoes on. Clear floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly shift your weight to your right foot. Pause.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay flat on the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–2:15 · Backward walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Backward walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Take normal-size steps backward, toe then heel.</td><td>Easier: Five small steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand stays on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow. Look where you're going first.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hand stays on the counter. Slow. Look where you're going first. **Easier:** Five small steps. **Harder:** Ten steps, slower.

**Safety callouts:** Only ever with a hand resting on the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:15–3:15 · Step over a towel

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Step over a towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step over the towel sideways with the near foot, then the other.</td><td>Easier: Flat towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift the knee. Clear the towel.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Lift the knee. Clear the towel. Hand on the counter. **Easier:** A flat towel instead of rolled. **Harder:** Step over forward and back, still holding the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:15–4:10 · Clock reach

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Clock reach</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Reach your free arm forward to 12 o'clock. Back to center.</td><td>Easier: Smaller reaches, front and side</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Follow your hand with your eyes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay planted.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you reach.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Follow your hand with your eyes. Feet stay planted. **Easier:** Smaller reaches, and only to the front and side. **Harder:** Stand on one foot while you reach to 12 o'clock, holding the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:10–5:20 · One-leg stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>One-leg stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to your left foot.</td><td>Easier: Toe stays on the floor</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly. Count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg. **Easier:** Just shift your weight onto one foot, keeping the other toe lightly on the floor. **Harder:** One hand hovering above the counter, then both hands hovering, right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:20–6:40 · Stair practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Stair practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk up one step at a time at a steady pace, whole foot on each step.</td><td>Easier: Bottom 3 steps only</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rail hand never lets go.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. Rest at the top as long as you like.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step. Rail hand never lets go. **Easier:** Just the bottom 3 steps, up and down. **Harder:** Two flights, or carry a light bag in the free hand.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain or unusual breathlessness on stairs: stop, sit, and call your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:40–7:25 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise up onto the balls of your feet, as high as is comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:25–8:00 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:00–8:25 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>New steps, same counter.</td><td></td></tr>

# BAL-B2 · Phase 2 (Build): Tai chi: three forms

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:25 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:25–2:55 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to the right foot while your right hand floats across in front of your face and your left hand floats low in front of your belly.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:55–4:25 · Brush knee

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Brush knee</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step forward with the left foot, heel first, into a short stance.</td><td>Easier: Arms only, feet together</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short step, not a lunge.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight moves slowly from back foot to front foot.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push forward.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Short step, not a lunge. Weight moves slowly from back foot to front foot. **Easier:** Arms only, feet together, one hand on the counter. **Harder:** Four steps across the room and back, near the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:25–6:05 · Parting the horse's mane

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Parting the horse's mane</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Imagine holding a ball at your chest, right hand on top.</td><td>Easier: Arms only, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short step.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow like honey.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as the arm sweeps up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Short step. Slow like honey. **Easier:** Arms only, feet together, holding the counter with one hand. **Harder:** Step forward across the room, left then right, near the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:05–6:55 · Drawing the bow

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Drawing the bow</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bring both hands in front of your chest.</td><td>Easier: Seated, arms only</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Knees over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grow tall through the top of the head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you draw the bow, in as you return.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Knees over toes. Grow tall through the top of the head. **Easier:** Sit tall in your chair and do the arm movement only. **Harder:** Bend your knees a little more (never below comfortable).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:55–7:55 · One-leg stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>One-leg stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to your left foot.</td><td>Easier: Toe stays on the floor</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly. Count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg. **Easier:** Just shift your weight onto one foot, keeping the other toe lightly on the floor. **Harder:** One hand hovering above the counter, then both hands hovering, right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:55–8:55 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Belly rises first.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft shoulders.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:55–9:20 · Close

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly shift your weight to your right foot. Pause.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay flat on the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–2:45 · Floor practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sturdy chair beside you. Towel down. Someone else home.</td><td>Floor practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Kneel with your hands on the chair. Rise through the front foot.</td><td>Easier: Half-kneel only, or chair stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push up. Stand still before you walk.</td><td>Only with a sturdy chair and someone home</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Practise getting up before you ever need to.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hands on the chair the whole time. Slow down. Up is a push, not a jump. **Easier:** Only the first step: lower into a half-kneel on the towel and come back up, holding the chair. Or skip the floor and do sit-to-stands. **Harder:** Iron: from kneeling, sit down onto the floor beside the chair, then roll to your knees and rise with the chair. Only with someone home.

**Safety callouts:** Only try the floor with a sturdy chair or sofa next to you and someone home. Recent hip or knee replacement, or severe knee arthritis: follow your surgeon's or physical therapist's guidance first. New knee? Kneeling may not be allowed yet. Ask your surgeon. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:45–3:45 · Step over a towel

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Step over a towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step over the towel sideways with the near foot, then the other.</td><td>Easier: Flat towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift the knee. Clear the towel.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Lift the knee. Clear the towel. Hand on the counter. **Easier:** A flat towel instead of rolled. **Harder:** Step over forward and back, still holding the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:45–4:45 · Big-step drill

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Big-step drill</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk 10 steps a little longer than your normal step.</td><td>Easier: Normal steps, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Heel, roll, push.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall. Eyes ahead.</td><td></td></tr>

</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Heel, roll, push. Tall. Eyes ahead. **Easier:** Normal-length steps, hand on the counter. **Harder:** 20 steps, a little faster.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:45–5:45 · Heel-to-toe walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel-to-toe walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step forward, placing your heel directly in front of the toes of the other foot.</td><td>Easier: Feet apart, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes forward, not down at your feet.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow is correct.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes forward, not down at your feet. Slow is correct. **Easier:** Walk with your feet slightly apart, not touching, holding the counter. **Harder:** Let your hand hover above the counter. Later: walk backward along the counter with one hand resting on it (normal steps).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:45–6:55 · One-leg stand + reach

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>One-leg stand + reach</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Reach your free arm forward to 12 o'clock. Back to center.</td><td>Easier: Smaller reaches, front and side</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Follow your hand with your eyes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay planted.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you reach.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Follow your hand with your eyes. Feet stay planted. **Easier:** Smaller reaches, and only to the front and side. **Harder:** Stand on one foot while you reach to 12 o'clock, holding the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet. Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

<tr><td>7:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit with feet slightly narrower than usual.</td><td>Easier: Hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Find your balance at the top before you move.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>

</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Find your balance at the top before you move. Slow down. **Easier:** Use your hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Feet together.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:40–8:15 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Balance & Steady Feet program | 9:20 | SET-PROM | C-TRAIN-B | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">

</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.
</div>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

# Where the numbers come from

Every number and health statement in this book traces to one of the entries below. They are the same evidence IDs our whole team uses (EVIDENCE.md). Grade A means a Cochrane review, a large meta-analysis or a guideline body. B means a single good trial or a small meta-analysis. C means an observational study: it shows a link, not cause and effect. D means lab, physiology or label data.


<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E09** (grade C). 10-second one-leg stance (free foot resting on the back of the other calf, arms at sides, 3 tries). 1,702 people aged 51–75. Failing it was linked with 84% higher all-cause mortality over about 7 years. Failure rates: about 18% at 61–65, about 37% at 66–70, over 50% at 71–75.

<p class="src">Source: Araújo et al., BJSM 2022 — https://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2022/june/tne-second-one-legged-stance.html</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E11** (grade A (tool)). CDC STEADI 30-second chair stand (17-inch chair, arms crossed), used in the CDC's older-adult screening. Below-average scores: men 60–64 <14, 65–69 <12, 70–74 <12, 75–79 <11, 80–84 <10, 85–89 <8, 90–94 <7. Women 60–64 <12, 65–69 <11, 70–74 <10, 75–79 <10, 80–84 <9, 85–89 <8, 90–94 <4. If arms are used to stand, the score is 0.

<p class="src">Source: CDC STEADI — https://www.cdc.gov/steadi/media/pdfs/STEADI-Assessment-30Sec-508.pdf</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E13** (grade A−). Otago Exercise Programme: a home programme of leg strengthening, balance exercises and walking designed for older adults, studied in 7 trials with 1,503 people (mean age 81.6). We use its exercise types and progressions; we make no outcome claim from it.

<p class="src">Source: Thomas et al., Age Ageing 2010 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK78898/</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E15** (grade B+). Tai chi vs physical therapy for knee osteoarthritis: 204 adults. Similar improvements in pain and function at 12 weeks, sustained to 52 weeks. Tai chi group had more improvement in depression and quality of life.

<p class="src">Source: Wang et al., Ann Intern Med 2016 — https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/research-results/study-shows-tai-chi-and-physical-therapy-were-equally-helpful-for-knee-osteoarthritis</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E17** (grade A−). Baduanjin/qigong in older adults: meta-analyses report better sleep quality and fewer depressive symptoms (moderate certainty, heterogeneous trials).

<p class="src">Source: Frontiers Public Health 2026 meta-analysis — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13501274/ ; qigong & sleep meta — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12757222/</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E41** (grade B (known literature)). Pain-monitoring model: during and after exercise, pain up to about 3/10 (we use a conservative threshold) is acceptable if it settles by the next morning and isn't trending up week to week.

<p class="src">Source: Thomeé, Phys Ther 1997; Silbernagel et al., Am J Sports Med 2007</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E42** (grade A (statement)). AHA scientific statement (2023): resistance training is recommended for adults with and without cardiovascular disease. It lowers blood pressure and improves glucose control and function. Avoid breath-holding (Valsalva). People with CVD should get individualized clearance.

<p class="src">Source: Paluch et al., Circulation 2024 — https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001189</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E43** (grade A (guideline)). Pre-exercise screening (ACSM 2015): anyone with symptoms of cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease (chest pain, unusual breathlessness, fainting) should get medical clearance before starting. Otherwise, light-to-moderate exercise can begin and progress.

<p class="src">Source: Riebe et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015 (known literature)</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E45** (grade B (known literature)). Getting-up-from-the-floor strategies can be taught to older adults. Practice it before you ever need it (backward chaining: kneel → half-kneel → stand, using sturdy furniture).

<p class="src">Source: Hofmeyer et al., J Am Geriatr Soc 2002 (floor-rise strategy training)</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E50** (grade A (tool)). CDC STEADI 4-Stage Balance Test: feet side by side, semi-tandem (instep beside big toe), tandem (heel to toe), one leg; up to 10 s each, stop at the first stage not held. The CDC uses the tandem stand as a screening checkpoint: under 10 s is worth discussing with a clinician.

<p class="src">Source: CDC STEADI — opened https://www.cdc.gov/steadi/media/pdfs/STEADI-Assessment-4Stage-508.pdf</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E51** (grade A (tool)). CDC STEADI Timed Up and Go: stand from a chair, walk 10 feet (3 m) at normal pace, turn, walk back, sit. The CDC uses 12 seconds or more as a screening threshold worth discussing with a clinician. Always have someone stand by.

<p class="src">Source: CDC STEADI — opened https://www.cdc.gov/steadi/media/pdfs/STEADI-Assessment-TUG-508.pdf</p>

</div>
